title: Intake Lens + Minimum Implementation Slate for High-touch Enterprise Requests
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: create a concise intake lens and a 'minimum implementation slate' (MIS) artifact that Sales/CS can use at first contact to (1) aggregate related feature asks, (2) rapidly classify feasibility and value, and (3) produce a 1-2 slide scope + recommended first-step (prototype/build/decline).

Problem: Sales currently sends heterogeneous ask formats (emails, spreadsheets, slide decks). PMs spend ~4-8 hours per high-touch ask just consolidating signals and building a hypothesis. This slows response time and increases missed opportunities for Dedicated/Private deals.

Goal: reduce PM first-touch consolidation time to <90 minutes per ask and provide a repeatable triage output that supports fast econ estimates for field and an engineering pre-check.

Deliverables:
- Intake Lens (one-page checklist + scoring rubric) to be used by CS AE or Solutions engineer during intake call.
- Minimum Implementation Slate (MIS): templated 1-slide scope with scope sketch, acceptance criteria, rough throughput and latency targets, and two cost levers (batching/quantization) flagged.
- Quick estimate matrix mapping ask types to recommended paths: Self-serve backlog, Prototype + eval, Dedicated sales engineer engagement, Decline/Redirect.

Non-goals: detailed technical spec, PRD, or final engineering estimates. Not intended to replace deep enterprise discovery for negotiated deals.

Success metrics:
- Triage time per ask reduced from median 5h to <=1.5h for high-touch cases.
- 30% faster first-response SLA from PMs to Sales for prioritized asks.
- 20% increase in prototype->paid conversion for requests surfaced via the MIS within 60 days.
scoping_checklist: Customer and account context: ARR band, compliance/regulatory constraints, expected ROI window
User journey and primary use case: single-call generation, batch inference, embedding pipeline, reranking
Data residency / security requirements: VPC/private deployment required, KMS/HSM?
Traffic profile: QPS, peak concurrency, typical sequence length distribution
Latency and SLO expectations: p50/p95 targets and acceptable tail behavior
Quality guardrails: sample prompts/test-cases, golden outputs, failure modes to avoid
Integration surface: API-only, SDK, UI/webhook, or agent/tooling connectivity
Must-have vs nice-to-have: minimal scope list (top 3) and stretch items
Proposed initial rollout path: canary in region X, dedicated capacity, or hosted API
Cost sensitivity and threshold: monthly token budget or per-token ceiling
quick_estimates: Prototype + eval: 2-4 sprint effort (PM + 1 Eng + SE), low infra commit (hosted API), expected cost: low-to-medium
Dedicated pilot: 4-8 sprint effort, needs capacity reservation and infra onboarding, expected cost: medium-to-high
Private/VPC: 8+ sprints, infra+security review + legal, expected cost: high
Self-serve/backlog: gather signals, schedule as backlog item, no immediate infra work
